candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: The strongest signal in this group is a mature B lymphocyte identity programme: CD79A forms the signal-transducing module of the B cell antigen receptor, STAP1 is a B cell adaptor that couples receptor engagement to downstream kinases, BTLA is an inhibitory receptor that raises the threshold for lymphocyte activation, and P2RX5 and prepronociceptin are expressed in B lineage cells and used to distinguish them. Together these support antigen recognition, tuned activation and the restraint that prevents autoreactivity. Alongside them sit components of cell-surface signalling and adhesion more broadly — caveolin-2 and the angiomotin-family scaffold AMOTL2 at membrane and junctional sites, a G protein gamma subunit, the growth hormone receptor, and SMAD1 carrying bone morphogenetic protein signals to the nucleus, with the secreted BMP antagonist chordin-like 1 opposing them. The set thus mixes lymphocyte receptor signalling with receptor-mediated growth and morphogenetic control.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes mark the megakaryocyte-platelet arm of haematopoiesis and the signalling that supports it. Platelet factor 4 is the archetypal alpha-granule chemokine released on platelet activation, junction plakoglobin anchors the cytoskeletal junctions and desmosomal-type adhesion used by these cells, and the G protein alpha-z subunit couples platelet ADP and adrenergic receptors to inhibition of adenylate cyclase, lowering cyclic AMP to permit aggregation. Monoacylglycerol lipase supplies arachidonic acid for eicosanoid production in the same setting. Alongside them sit regulators of progenitor commitment and marrow stromal support: the transcription factors MEF2C and ZNF423, the chromatin-associated MLLT3, and PDGFRA with the secreted modulators CRIM1 and FSTL1, which tune growth factor and BMP/TGF-beta input. Together the set describes how progenitors are specified toward thrombopoiesis and how the resulting platelets achieve haemostasis; its failure underlies bleeding and thrombotic disorders.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: Granulocyte maturation in the bone marrow, and the antimicrobial cargo that neutrophils acquire as they mature, is the theme here. Promyelocytes and myelocytes load their granules with proteins that will later be deployed against bacteria: a lipopolysaccharide-binding bactericidal protein of the BPI family, the adipokine-like secreted factor resistin, prokineticin 2, the soluble pattern-recognition molecule pentraxin 3, and a haematopoietic growth factor of the CLEC11A type that supports progenitor expansion. Alongside them sit regulators that hold inflammatory signalling in check, including the kinase-dead IRAK family member IRAK3, and transport and lipid-remodelling enzymes such as the organic cation/ergothioneine transporter SLC22A4 and a lysophospholipid acyltransferase. A CDK inhibitor of the INK4 family and a linker histone variant point to the exit from proliferation that accompanies terminal differentiation. Together these define innate myeloid effector capacity, whose loss leaves recurrent bacterial infection.

candidates.name: Hox cluster VI
candidates.description: HOX genes encode homeodomain transcription factors that assign positional identity along the head-to-tail axis of the embryo, and this grouping draws on members of the HOXA and HOXB clusters spanning anterior paralogues such as HOXA2, HOXA3 and HOXB2 through to more posterior HOXA9, HOXA10 and HOXB9. Their ordered, colinear expression instructs hindbrain segmentation, branchial arch and craniofacial derivatives, vertebral and limb pattern, and the regionalisation of the urogenital tract. The same factors act after development in haematopoietic progenitors, where HOXA9 and HOXA10 sustain self-renewal and proliferation; their inappropriate reactivation, often through mixed-lineage leukaemia fusions, drives acute leukaemia, while loss-of-function mutations produce limb and genital malformations. Activity depends on retinoic acid signalling upstream and on chromatin-level control by Polycomb and trithorax complexes to keep cluster expression appropriately restricted, with cofactors shaping DNA-binding specificity.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: Intestinal crypt epithelium maintained by Wnt signalling is what these genes describe: a stem and progenitor programme of the colonic crypt base together with markers of the differentiating epithelium above it. It sustains the continuous renewal of the gut lining, and its inappropriate reactivation underlies colorectal adenoma and carcinoma, where the same transcripts serve as tumour markers. Several members are direct Wnt/beta-catenin targets s ASCL2 specifies and reinforces stem cell identity, AXIN2 and RNF43 act as negative feedback on the pathway itself, RNF43 by ubiquitinating Frizzled receptors, and EPHB2 expression follows the crypt-axis gradient that sorts cells to their correct position. CDCA7 links the programme to proliferation, while GPX2, CEACAM5, MUC3B and TSPAN8 reflect mucosal antioxidant defence, mucin production and the apical surface of the absorptive epithelium.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This grouping describes the transcriptional programme of immature myeloid progenitors in the bone marrow, the stage at which granulocyte, mast cell and erythroid potential is still being resolved and primary granule proteins are first made. Its hallmark products are the azurophilic granule enzymes myeloperoxidase and neutrophil elastase, together with the mast cell protease carboxypeptidase A3 and the promyelocyte membrane marker MS4A3, so the signature marks promyelocytes and their close relatives rather than mature blood cells. Lineage transcription factors TAL1 and NFE2 act alongside proliferative drive from CDK6 and niche cues such as JAG1, PDGFC and the stem cell growth factor CLEC11A, while SLC40A1 exports iron for haem synthesis. Loss or distortion of this programme underlies congenital neutropenias and is the state in which acute myeloid leukaemia blasts are arrested.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes outline a mesenchymal, mechanoresponsive fibroblast programme in which YAP and its paralogue TAZ (WWTR1) convert cytoskeletal tension and matrix stiffness into transcription of matricellular and adhesion genes. CYR61 is a canonical YAP/TAZ target, and alongside collagen III, follistatin-like 1, caveolin-1 and VCAM1 it marks cells that build and remodel connective tissue and support leukocyte and progenitor traffic. Growth factor and cytokine receptors such as PDGFRA and OSMR, together with the chemokine CXCL12, define the stromal niche signals these cells emit and receive, while ERRFI1 restrains EGF receptor output and EPS8 couples receptor signalling to actin. The same circuitry drives wound repair and alveolar and vascular stromal maintenance, and its persistent activation underlies fibrosis and the stiff, invasion-permissive stroma of tumours.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes form a brake system on leukocyte activation, tuning how strongly lymphocytes and myeloid cells respond to antigen receptor, Toll-like and cytokine receptor engagement. Restraint of this kind sets thresholds for activation, prevents autoimmunity and chronic inflammation, and is also what tumours exploit to blunt T cell responses, making several members attractive immunotherapy targets. Mechanistically the set mixes activating and dampening arms: VAV1 is a Rac/Rho exchange factor downstream of antigen receptors, while ARHGAP15 and ARHGAP4 act as GTPase-activating proteins that switch such Rho-family signalling off. DGKZ consumes diacylglycerol to terminate protein kinase C and Ras signalling; MAP4K1 (HPK1) phosphorylates the adaptor SLP-76 to disassemble receptor signalosomes; SIGIRR blocks interleukin-1 and Toll-like receptor output. LYN, HCLS1, LPXN and beta-arrestin 2 couple these events to cytoskeletal and inhibitory-receptor responses, with GATA3 shaping lymphoid identity.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This grouping describes lymphocyte activation within organised lymphoid tissue, the process by which antigen-experienced B and T cells are positioned, co-stimulated and driven toward antibody secretion. It underlies germinal centre reactions and the generation of plasma cells, and its components are the surface markers used to identify activated and malignant lymphoid cells. A stromal chemokine and an oxysterol-sensing receptor guide migration into and within follicles, while CD27 and the SLAM-family receptors LY9 and SLAMF7 provide co-stimulatory contacts between lymphocytes. Downstream survival signalling through an NF-κB-associated ubiquitin ligase, IL-15 support, and the transcription factor IRF4 commit cells to effector and plasma-cell fates, reflected here in immunoglobulin kappa transcripts. Interferon-responsive elements including a peptide transporter for MHC class I loading tie the same tissue to cytotoxic T cell surveillance; loss of these interactions produces immunodeficiency with poor antibody responses.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This is a heterogeneous grouping rather than a single mechanism, but its members converge on the theme of cell-type-specific differentiation and the signalling that supports it. Transcriptional regulators dominate one arm: SOX15 and TCF15 act in mesodermal and skeletal muscle lineage specification, while CDKN2B encodes a cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor of the INK4 family that restrains G1 progression and links differentiation to cell cycle exit, a function lost in many tumours. A neuronal arm includes the RNA-binding protein ELAVL3, which stabilises transcripts in neurons, the microtubule plus-end tracking protein MAPRE3, and the gamma isoform of protein kinase C, whose mutation causes spinocerebellar ataxia. Others reflect blood and vascular specialisation: GP1BB contributes to the platelet von Willebrand factor receptor, and FUT7 builds the fucosylated selectin ligands that let leukocytes roll on endothelium.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes converge on the regulation of gene expression at the steps between transcription and protein turnover. Cyclin T2 partners CDK9 in the elongation kinase that releases paused RNA polymerase II, while cyclin C works within the Mediator kinase module that gates promoter engagement, and ARID4A and SP3 act on chromatin and promoter DNA to set which genes are read. The CLK1 kinase phosphorylates SR-family splicing factors, and a splicing regulator of that family is present, linking transcriptional output to how transcripts are spliced. A second arm handles protein fate: RING ubiquitin ligases, a proteasomal ATPase subunit, and the deubiquitinase USP1, which removes monoubiquitin from FANCD2 and PCNA and so restrains DNA damage tolerance. Together the set reflects how proliferating cells couple transcriptional programmes, RNA processing, and regulated degradation, with membrane and mitochondrial components at the periphery.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes mark the erythroid-megakaryocytic branch of hematopoiesis, the programme by which bone marrow progenitors commit to making red cells and platelets rather than lymphoid or granulocytic fates. Its transcriptional core is a TAL1-GFI1B axis that drives erythroid gene expression while restraining progenitor proliferation; loss of either blocks red cell production, and GFI1B mutation causes a bleeding disorder with malformed platelets. Downstream effectors give the lineage its identity: hemogen accompanies erythroid maturation, GMPR shapes the guanine nucleotide pool of erythroid cells, and the XK membrane protein partners with the Kell blood group antigen, its absence producing McLeod syndrome with acanthocytic red cells. Cytoskeletal and adhesion components such as ACTN1 and TNS1 support megakaryocyte and platelet structure, ACTN1 mutations causing inherited macrothrombocytopenia, while MS4A3 marks the granulocyte-monocyte progenitor compartment nearby.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This grouping centres on membrane traffic through the Golgi and the machinery that buds, tethers and fuses transport vesicles, the route by which secretory and lysosomal cargo reaches its destination. Its outputs are secretion, receptor recycling and delivery of hydrolases such as cathepsin D to lysosomes; when it falters, cargo is mislocalised and organelle identity degrades. A large GEF acting on ARF GTPases recruits the COPI coat for retrograde transport, a coat subunit is represented directly, and an NSF attachment protein supports SNARE complex disassembly after fusion, while a dynamin GTPase pinches off budding carriers. Heterotrimeric G protein subunits and phosphatase and kinase components add regulatory input, and lipid-modifying enzymes including a neuropathy target esterase-type lysophospholipase and an S-acyl protein thioesterase tune membrane lipid and palmitoylation states that govern where proteins reside.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This grouping brings together nuclear regulators of chromatin and transcription with a smaller set of membrane and metabolic enzymes, and is best read as a broad housekeeping module supporting gene expression and genome maintenance. On the nuclear side, SMARCA5 is the ATPase of ISWI-type nucleosome remodelling complexes that space nucleosomes during replication and repair; TLK1 phosphorylates histone chaperones to couple chromatin assembly to S phase; USP1 removes ubiquitin from FANCD2 and PCNA to terminate DNA damage tolerance and interstrand crosslink repair; ATF2, TCERG1 and SFRS12 act on transcription and splicing, and ZMYM2 and RNF6 contribute transcriptional repression and ubiquitin ligation. Alongside these, PIKFYVE generates PI(3,5)P2 for endolysosomal membrane dynamics, ACBD3 organises Golgi signalling, and AGL and PANK3 serve glycogen debranching and coenzyme A synthesis. Loss of such functions impairs replication-coupled chromatin assembly, repair fidelity and basic metabolic supply.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes mark the differentiated absorptive and secretory epithelium of the gastrointestinal tract, the barrier layer that absorbs nutrients, detoxifies luminal xenobiotics and presents a glycan-coated surface to the microbiota. Adhesion and junctional components such as EPCAM and FERMT1 hold the sheet together, while lineage transcription factors including FOXA3 and KLF5 drive and maintain the differentiated state; loss of these programmes underlies barrier failure, inflammatory bowel disease and the dedifferentiation seen in colorectal cancer, where CEACAM and galectin-4 expression is routinely used as an epithelial marker. A large glycosyltransferase and fucosylation component (B3GNT3, B3GNT5, FUT3, GMDS, ST3GAL6) builds the mucin and blood-group-related glycans of the apical surface. Additional members handle lipid binding and handling, iron export, oxidative defence through GPX2 and NOX1, and nuclear-receptor-driven drug metabolism.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: Membrane traffic and organelle remodelling form the common thread here: newly folded cargo leaves the endoplasmic reticulum in COPII-coated vesicles built from SEC23A and SEC24B, is delivered through early endosomes marked by the tethering factor EEA1, and reaches the plasma membrane by SNARE-directed fusion, with STXBP3 acting among the Sec1/Munc18-family regulators of that step. Lipid composition and cytoskeletal geometry are managed alongside cargo flow: the inositol phosphatase SYNJ1 dephosphorylates PI(4,5)P2 to uncoat vesicles after endocytosis, TMEM30A serves as the accessory subunit that allows P4-ATPase flippases to translocate aminophospholipids across bilayers, and the microtubule-severing ATPase SPAST shapes tubules and axonal microtubule arrays. Additional members touch nuclear pore transport, transcriptional control by RB1, and ADAM9-mediated ectodomain shedding, linking secretory and endocytic capacity to cell surface signalling, neuronal maintenance and proliferation control.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes outline the transcriptional and structural programme that gives absorptive epithelium of the gut and kidney tubule its identity: a polarized brush-border cell that moves solutes across a sealed barrier. HNF4G, TFAP2C and SIX4 act as lineage-directing transcription factors, while CLDN2 builds a cation- and water-permeable tight junction pore that sets paracellular leakiness, and SLC3A1 supplies the heavy subunit of the transporter that reabsorbs cystine and dibasic amino acids — its loss causes cystinuria with kidney stones. Scaffolding and PDZ-domain proteins such as USH1C (harmonin), GIPC2 and the clarin-family membrane protein CLRN3 organize apical membrane and microvillar structure, and the E3 ligase RNF186 restrains inflammatory signalling in intestinal epithelium, a link that makes this module relevant to ulcerative colitis susceptibility and to barrier failure more broadly.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes sketch a morphogen-driven programme that patterns mesenchymal tissue and steers progenitors toward bone, cartilage, skin and blood-supporting fates. BMP signalling sits at its centre: SMAD1 carries the receptor signal to the nucleus, ZNF521 acts as a nuclear cofactor tuning that output in skeletal and haematopoietic progenitors, while secreted GREM1 antagonises BMP ligands to keep niches permissive, and INHBA contributes an activin/TGF-beta arm through its own receptor-SMAD route. HHIP dampens Hedgehog signalling, so two major developmental gradients are held in check simultaneously by extracellular inhibitors. Downstream and in parallel, the Rac exchange factor TIAM1 and protein kinase C eta couple these cues to cytoskeletal remodelling and epithelial differentiation, ADAM12 remodels matrix and sheds surface proteins, and the transcriptional regulators RORA and BCL11B impose lineage identity. Imbalance here underlies skeletal dysplasia, fibrosis and tumour stroma behaviour.

candidates.name: TBA (source: naive B cells)
candidates.description: This is a marker grouping derived from naive B cells, the resting, antigen-inexperienced lymphocytes that circulate after bone marrow development and before germinal centre entry, and whose activation initiates antibody responses. The genes assembled here do not form a coherent biochemical module: they span an innate immune regulator of pyrin-driven inflammasome activity and febrile inflammation, a type I interferon gene, a secreted metalloproteinase of the ADAMTS family, potassium channel tetramerisation-domain and transmembrane proteins, a POU-family transcription factor, a hepatic tyrosine aminotransferase, olfactory receptor and testis-expressed loci, and several pseudogene or low-confidence transcripts. The unifying theme is therefore expression pattern rather than shared mechanism, and the set is best read as a transcriptional signature distinguishing the naive B cell state from activated, memory and plasma cell stages, with interferon and inflammasome components hinting at the innate signalling context in which such cells are poised to respond.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: No single process unites these genes; they instead sample several core housekeeping systems that any proliferating cell depends on. One arm is growth-factor signalling through small GTPases: NRAS relays receptor input to MAP kinase and PI3K routes, RAP2C acts in Ras-family signalling to cytoskeletal and polarity effectors, and PIK3C2A generates phosphoinositides that direct membrane traffic and endocytosis. A second arm handles protein biogenesis and secretion, with SRP9 targeting nascent chains to the endoplasmic reticulum and SEC23A forming part of the COPII coat that buds cargo toward the Golgi; loss of SEC23A activity underlies a craniofacial dysplasia. A third arm is nuclear and transcriptional: SP3 and TCF12 are DNA-binding regulators of developmental gene programmes, CCNC partners a kinase in transcriptional control, and AEBP2 associates with Polycomb repressive complex 2. RNF6 contributes ubiquitin-dependent turnover.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This grouping centres on control of cell survival and proliferation decisions during tissue growth and differentiation. Two hubs stand out: the retinoblastoma protein RB1, which restrains the G1/S transition by holding E2F-dependent transcription in check and whose loss underlies retinoblastoma and many sporadic cancers, and BCL2L1, an anti-apoptotic member of the BCL2 family that guards mitochondrial outer membrane integrity and blocks cytochrome c release. Around them sit transcriptional regulators (ATF1, SP3), the RNA-binding protein RBM38 and the splicing regulator MBNL3, which impose post-transcriptional layers on the same programme, alongside ubiquitin ligases such as RNF6 and HERC4 that set protein turnover. SLC7A5 imports large neutral amino acids to support anabolic growth, while SPAST severs microtubules, a function whose failure causes hereditary spastic paraplegia.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes mark the resident fibroblast and perivascular stromal compartment of connective tissue, the cell population that builds and remodels extracellular matrix and supplies growth signals to neighbouring epithelium, endothelium and immune cells. Matrix and matrix-associated products such as tenascin C, ECM2, OLFML3 and the BMP antagonist chordin-like 1 shape tissue architecture and the diffusion of morphogens, while locally produced complement components C1S and C7 give stroma a role in innate immune surveillance. Receptors for PDGF (PDGFRA, PDGFRB), growth hormone, oncostatin M and GDNF family ligands let these cells respond to injury, inflammatory and endocrine cues, and IGF2 provides paracrine growth support. Programmes of this kind underlie wound healing and tissue growth, and their persistent activation produces fibrosis and the tumour-supporting stroma of carcinomas.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes mark a perivascular stromal and endothelial compartment, the interface where capillaries meet connective tissue matrix. Secreted matrix components such as EFEMP1 (fibulin-3) and ECM2 organise the basement membrane and elastic fibre environment that keeps vessels and surrounding tissue mechanically coherent, while IL33 acts both as a nuclear factor in endothelium and, when released from damaged cells, as an alarmin that recruits type 2 immune responses. Several adhesion G protein-coupled receptors are represented, including ELTD1/ADGRL4, which is endothelial and shapes angiogenic sprouting, and GPR116/ADGRF5, required for alveolar surfactant homeostasis; GNG12 supplies a G protein gamma subunit for such signalling, and MPDZ scaffolds junctional complexes. Together the set describes matrix deposition, junction organisation and vascular-stromal crosstalk, processes underlying tissue remodelling, fibrosis and vessel integrity.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: The dominant theme here is chromatin-based control of gene expression coupled to ubiquitin-dependent protein regulation. Polycomb components BMI1 and EED, the histone chaperone ANP32E, the chromatin remodeller SMARCA5 and the histone-binding MORF4L2 together repress or reposition nucleosomes at developmental and proliferation genes, keeping stem and progenitor identity stable and restraining tumour suppressor loci such as the CDKN2A region. Alongside them sit ubiquitin pathway components — the CUL5 scaffold and the RING ligases RNF6 and RNF138 — that set protein turnover and contribute to DNA damage responses, and a transcription-associated cyclin partner, CCNC. A second group acts in the secretory pathway and endoplasmic reticulum: SRP9 in cotranslational targeting, SEC63 in translocation, the thiol oxidoreductase TMX1, the selenoprotein SEP15 and the phosphoinositide phosphatase SACM1L. The set therefore spans nuclear gene silencing, regulated proteolysis and ER protein folding and quality control.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes read as the secretory programme of a mesenchymal stromal or fibroblast-like cell that builds and maintains tissue architecture and supports the cells embedded in it. CXCL12 is the chemokine by which such stroma recruits and retains haematopoietic progenitors and lymphocytes, while IGF1 with its carrier IGFBP3 sets local growth-factor availability, FRZB tunes Wnt signalling as a secreted antagonist, and complement component C7 and the secreted nuclease DNASE1L3 contribute to clearance of extracellular debris and immune tone. Aquaporin-1 handles water permeability and connexin-43 couples neighbouring cells through gap junctions, features of perivascular and connective tissue. SNAI2 acts as the transcriptional regulator holding the mesenchymal state and driving epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, and ALDH1A3 supplies retinoic acid for local patterning. Together this describes niche support, matrix remodelling and the fibroblast responses that turn into fibrosis or tumour stroma when sustained.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: A mixed immune-expression module centred on mononuclear leukocyte identity and trafficking, combining chemokine receptors, GTPase-of-immunity-associated proteins and transcriptional regulators. Monocyte and macrophage recruitment to inflamed tissue depends on CCR2 and CX3CR1, whose ligands direct patrolling and infiltrating cells to vessel walls and injured sites; loss of this axis blunts inflammatory monocyte egress from bone marrow and reshapes atherosclerotic and neuroinflammatory disease. The GIMAP proteins act in lymphocyte survival and homeostasis, linking the set to T cell persistence as well as myeloid function. Signalling and feedback components include the IL-1 receptor accessory protein required for interleukin-1 responses, the MAPK phosphatase DUSP4 that dampens kinase output, the TNF-family receptor FN14, and the immediate-early factor NR4A3. Numerous KRAB-type zinc finger proteins and the repressor HIC1 suggest accompanying transcriptional control, alongside metabolic and autophagy-related members.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: Circulating monocytes find their way into tissue by reading chemokine gradients, and the two receptors that anchor this group, CCR2 and CX3CR1, are the pair that defines the classical and non-classical monocyte subsets and governs their recruitment to inflamed vessel walls, injured tissue and the brain, where they become macrophages or microglia. Loss or blockade of this axis limits atherosclerotic plaque myeloid influx and blunts inflammatory infiltration, which is why it is a longstanding drug target. Alongside the receptors sit immediate-early transcriptional responses, with the AP-1 component FOSL1 and the orphan nuclear receptor NR4A3 coupling receptor engagement to changes in gene expression that set monocyte activation state and survival. Additional zinc-finger factors and the immune-associated GTPase-like GIMAP6 suggest accompanying transcriptional and lymphoid-myeloid regulatory control rather than chemotaxis alone.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: Iron handling, hypoxic adaptation and membrane lipid composition converge here on a cell's vulnerability to iron-dependent oxidative death. Iron-regulatory protein 2 sets the labile iron pool by controlling ferritin and transferrin receptor messages post-transcriptionally, while ACSL4 activates polyunsaturated fatty acids for incorporation into phospholipids and thereby supplies the peroxidation substrate that commits a cell to ferroptosis. HIF1A couples the same chemistry to oxygen availability, and SIRT1, ATF2 and TCF12 provide NAD-dependent and transcriptional arms that tune stress responses and metabolic output. Additional members act on membrane and cytoskeletal traffic: SYNJ1 dephosphorylates phosphoinositides during synaptic vesicle recycling, OSTM1 partners the lysosomal chloride-proton exchanger required for bone resorption, and ROCK1 drives actomyosin contraction. The shared theme is redox- and iron-sensitive control of cell survival, relevant to neurodegeneration, ischaemic injury and tumour cell death.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes mark the epithelial identity programme of stratified and glandular epithelia, particularly of the gastrointestinal tract, and its coordinated regulation of differentiation, adhesion and mucosal barrier function. Transcription factors set the programme: CDX1 specifies intestinal identity and is a determinant of intestinal metaplasia when expressed in stomach or oesophagus, while KLF5 and the ETS factor EHF drive proliferation and maturation of epithelial progenitors. Their downstream output includes structural components of cell-cell and cell-matrix junctions, with the plakophilin PKP3 in desmosomes and ladinin anchoring basal cells to the basement membrane, alongside the FXYD3 ion-transport modulator and glycosylation enzymes GALNT3 and GMDS that build mucin-type O-glycans and fucosylated surface glycans. TRIM29 ties the programme to keratinocyte differentiation and DNA-damage responses. Persistent activation of these factors is a recurring feature of carcinomas of epithelial origin, where they sustain tumour cell proliferation and lineage identity.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This grouping centres on TGF-β/BMP superfamily signalling and its downstream control of cell fate and growth arrest. BMP4 and the activin-like receptor ACVR1C transmit ligand binding into Smad-dependent transcription, with the repulsive guidance molecule RGMA acting as a BMP co-receptor, while CDKN2B encodes the p15 cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor that enforces the cytostatic response to these ligands in epithelial and haematopoietic cells. A parallel stress-kinase arm, built from MAP3K10 and the JNK-activating kinase MAP2K7, couples the same inputs to AP-1-type transcription and to FOXO4-mediated stress and survival control. Effectors of differentiation appear alongside: myocardin drives smooth muscle gene expression, WNT11 and FOXL1 pattern mesenchymal tissue, and DLG4 and APLP1 tie the module to synaptic scaffolding. Such signalling shapes vascular and mesenchymal development, and its loss contributes to tumour growth and fibrotic remodelling.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: A heterogeneous module in which scaffolded stress-kinase signalling meets secretory and growth control. Its clearest core is a JNK pathway assembly: a mixed-lineage kinase of the MAP3K family together with a JNK-interacting scaffold protein organises upstream kinases into a complex, and such scaffolds concentrate stress signalling at defined membrane and synaptic sites, where the PDZ scaffold PSD-95 anchors receptors and channels in excitatory postsynaptic densities and an ARF6 guanine-nucleotide exchange factor directs membrane traffic and cortical remodelling. Other members tie this to endocrine and proliferative outcomes: insulin as the hormonal output of beta cells, a calcium-activated monovalent cation channel that shapes membrane depolarisation and excitability, a CARD-containing adaptor feeding NF-kB activation, a cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor restraining G1 progression, and a Wnt ligand plus a forkhead factor acting in mesenchymal patterning. Failures in such couplings contribute to impaired insulin release, altered excitability, and dysregulated growth.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This grouping centres on regulators of neuronal and progenitor cell fate, linking chromatin-level transcriptional control to membrane and cytoskeletal signalling. Several members set how readily a cell proliferates or differentiates: the retinoblastoma protein restrains the G1-to-S transition, a histone deacetylase and a Paf1 complex subunit shape transcription elongation and repression, and a basic helix-loop-helix factor drives neural and mesenchymal differentiation programmes. Against that, a protein tyrosine phosphatase relays growth factor input into Ras-ERK signalling, while ATG5 commits membranes to autophagosome formation and a synaptic phosphoinositide phosphatase recycles vesicles at nerve terminals. The prion protein and a synaptic glycoprotein act at the neuronal surface. Metabolic and salvage enzymes supply the reducing and nucleotide chemistry these processes depend on, and loss of the purine salvage enzyme produces the neurological features of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: The grouping is anchored on post-transcriptional and transcriptional control of gene expression in neural and developing tissues. Three sequence-specific RNA-binding proteins carry much of its identity: the neuronal ELAV-family protein ELAVL3 and the cytoplasmic polyadenylation element binding protein CPEB3 govern stability, localisation and translation of mRNAs in neurons, where CPEB3 acts on transcripts encoding glutamate receptor subunits and contributes to synaptic plasticity and memory, while YBX1 is a broadly acting mRNA packaging and translational regulator. Their targets and partners appear alongside them: the obligatory NMDA receptor subunit GRIN1, which mediates calcium influx at excitatory synapses, and the ARF6 activator PSD, which drives membrane trafficking in neurites. Homeobox and SRY-box transcription factors such as EVX1, TCF15 and SOX15 place the same logic in embryonic patterning and muscle progenitors, and ARMC9 links the set to ciliary function, whose loss causes cerebellar malformation.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes mark the antimicrobial granule programme of neutrophils, the arsenal that granulocytes build during maturation in bone marrow and deploy against bacteria and fungi at sites of infection. BPI binds and permeabilises Gram-negative outer membranes through its affinity for lipopolysaccharide, lipocalin 2 sequesters bacterial siderophores to starve microbes of iron, and olfactomedin 4 defines a distinct subset of neutrophil specific granules; CEACAM8 is a surface glycoprotein used routinely to identify granulocytes and their precursors. Together they represent oxygen-independent killing and nutritional immunity rather than the respiratory burst. Supporting members point to vesicle handling and membrane lipid traffic during granule formation and exocytosis, while CARD11 contributes to antigen receptor-driven NF-κB signalling in lymphocytes. Loss or dilution of this granule content, as in myeloid maturation defects, leaves patients prone to recurrent pyogenic infection.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes outline the interface between proliferative arrest and inflammatory secretion that characterises cellular senescence. On the chromatin side, the Polycomb component BMI1 is part of the complex that ubiquitinates histone H2A to silence the CDKN2A locus and keep cells cycling, while the deubiquitinase USP16 removes that mark and opposes it, so the balance between them sets how readily a cell exits the cycle. Mitotic surveillance and division geometry are represented by the spindle checkpoint protein BUB3, the augmin subunit HAUS3, the phosphatase catalytic subunit PPP1CC and the p53-inducible cyclin CCNG1, linking damage and mis-segregation to arrest. Arrested cells then secrete IL1A, IL1B, oncostatin M and epiregulin, cytokines and growth factors that remodel the local tissue, recruit immune cells and can either reinforce tumour suppression or promote age-related inflammation and tumour progression.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes converge on integrin-based adhesion and the cytoskeletal signalling that lets cells grip and respond to their extracellular matrix, with a supporting cast of metabolic and gene-regulatory proteins. Talin links activated integrin tails to actin, integrin-linked kinase couples the adhesion complex to downstream survival and contractility signalling, and a Rho GDP-dissociation inhibitor restrains Rho-family GTPases so that actin remodelling is switched rather than constant; a microtubule-associated protein and the SNARE-recycling factor alpha-SNAP tie the same events to cytoskeletal turnover and membrane fusion. NBEAL2 is required for platelet alpha-granule biogenesis, and TGFB1 is a principal granule cargo and matrix-remodelling cytokine, placing part of this biology in platelet adhesion, secretion and wound repair. Additional components handle arginine methylation, NADPH and redox balance, oxidative carbon flux, and lipid-sensing transcriptional control, the metabolic backdrop on which adhesion and secretion depend.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes outline the terminal stages of erythroid differentiation, in which a committed progenitor remodels its membrane and cytoskeleton, condenses and expels its nucleus, and emerges as a deformable red cell able to survive repeated passage through capillaries and the spleen. Structural components dominate: beta-spectrin builds the membrane skeleton beneath the lipid bilayer, pleckstrin-2 and cortactin drive the actin rearrangements required for enucleation and cell shaping, and XK forms a disulphide-linked complex with the Kell glycoprotein at the erythrocyte surface. Transcriptional input from NFIA and PBX1 helps set the balance between erythroid and other myeloid fates, while GMPR and monoglyceride lipase reflect the nucleotide and lipid metabolism of maturing red cells. Loss of skeletal components causes hereditary spherocytosis and haemolytic anaemia; loss of XK produces acanthocytic red cells with neurological degeneration.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes converge on nuclear organisation and nucleocytoplasmic traffic: chromatin architecture, mRNA processing, ribosome biogenesis and export of cargo through the nuclear pore. CTCF and the cohesin subunit SMC1A together define chromatin loop boundaries and insulate promoters from inappropriate enhancers, which is how genome folding is translated into transcriptional output; ADNP and ATF1 act on transcription, the latter as a CREB-family factor responding to cAMP signalling. XPO1 exports proteins and ribonucleoprotein cargo out of the nucleus, NUP37 is a component of the nuclear pore scaffold, CRNKL1 contributes to spliceosomal function and NOC3L to pre-ribosome maturation, while centrin-3 links to centrosome duplication and a regulatory subunit of protein phosphatase 2A modulates mitotic progression. Collectively the set describes the interface between nuclear structure, gene expression and cell division, processes whose disruption drives developmental disorders and chromosomal instability in cancer.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes outline an endothelial identity and blood-vessel morphogenesis programme, of the kind that distinguishes vascular endothelium and sets arterial versus venous character during angiogenic remodelling. Its output is a patent, correctly patterned vascular network: guidance receptors such as neuropilin-1 and the fibronectin leucine-rich repeat protein FLRT2 read angiogenic and adhesive cues, adhesion-family GPCRs enriched in endothelium (ADGRL4/ELTD1, ADGRL2) tune sprouting behaviour, and the soluble guanylate cyclase alpha subunit places nitric oxide-cGMP signalling and vessel tone in the same module. Downstream, the Hippo pathway transcriptional coactivators YAP1 and WWTR1/TAZ convert junctional and flow-derived mechanical information into growth and junction remodelling, while ARHGAP29 restrains RhoA to permit cytoskeletal and lumen formation and the scaffold MPDZ supports apical junction organisation. The nuclear receptor NR2F2 contributes venous specification, and failure of such regulation yields vascular malformation and impaired sprouting.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes converge on myeloid and platelet function, where surface signalling is translated into changes in the actin cytoskeleton and in gene expression. The Src-family kinase LYN sits at the top of immunoreceptor and integrin signalling in leukocytes and platelets, setting both activating and inhibitory tone, while LST1 is an immune-cell transmembrane protein that shapes membrane protrusions and cell-cell contact. MRVI1 couples nitric oxide-driven cGMP signalling to inhibition of calcium release from intracellular stores, a brake on platelet activation. CEBPB provides the transcriptional arm, driving inflammatory and granulocyte-macrophage differentiation programmes, and PDLIM7 and XPO6 act on actin organisation, the latter exporting actin from the nucleus. Also represented are phospholipid synthesis, autophagy-related trafficking and tRNA splicing activities that support these cells, making the group a mixture of activation signalling, cytoskeletal control and housekeeping capacity.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: The genes here sketch late erythroid differentiation and the assembly of the red cell surface. Erythropoiesis matters because it supplies the circulating oxygen carriers, and its transcriptional and membrane components determine both red cell mechanical resilience and the antigens that decide transfusion compatibility. Transcriptional regulators such as NFIA and PBX1 bias progenitors toward the erythroid rather than granulocytic fate, while cytoskeletal and adhesion proteins including the tropomodulin TMOD1, non-muscle myosin MYH10 and E-cadherin shape the actin-spectrin membrane skeleton and the erythroblastic island contacts with macrophages. Two membrane transporters carry clinically recognised blood group antigens: the urea transporter SLC14A1 and the xenobiotic efflux pump ABCG2, the latter also a marker of stem and progenitor populations. Loss of the structural arm of this programme produces fragile erythrocytes and haemolytic anaemia, while its surface proteins underlie alloimmunisation.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This grouping centres on stress-activated transcriptional signalling and its supporting membrane and metabolic machinery. Its recognisable core is the kinase TAK1 (MAP3K7) acting upstream of the CREB/ATF family factors ATF1 and ATF2, a route by which cytokine, TGF-beta and stress inputs are converted into changes in gene expression governing inflammation, survival and differentiation; loss of TAK1 signalling causes inflammatory and developmental failure. Around this sit components of vesicular and secretory biology, including the early endosome tether EEA1 that organises incoming cargo on Rab5-positive membranes, the P4-ATPase ATP11C that flips phosphatidylserine to maintain plasma membrane asymmetry and is required for B lymphopoiesis and erythrocyte integrity, and the calcium-binding ER protein RCN2. Post-transcriptional and metabolic contributors include the splicing regulator MBNL2, the zinc-finger factors IKZF5 and ZBTB41, and glycogen debranching enzyme AGL, whose deficiency causes glycogen storage disease type III.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This grouping centres on adaptor and scaffold proteins that set the gain of growth-factor and inflammatory signalling rather than carrying it themselves. Two arms dominate. One is NF- f0bB control: IKK f41 (CHUK) phosphorylates inhibitors of NF- f0bB to license inflammatory and survival transcription, while BAG4 and ZFAND6 act at TNF receptor complexes to restrain death-domain signalling. The other is BMP/TGF- f42 output, where the type II receptor BMPR2 initiates SMAD phosphorylation and the ubiquitin ligase RNF111 (Arkadia) degrades the inhibitory SMAD7 to sustain it; loss-of-function in BMPR2 underlies heritable pulmonary arterial hypertension. Linking these to cell-cycle and metabolic decisions are RB1, which enforces the restriction point, the mTOR effector kinase S6K1, and the NAD-dependent deacetylase SIRT1. Anchoring and GEF proteins such as AKAP11, ARFGEF2 and RAPGEF6 localise kinase and small-GTPase activity within this network.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: The dominant theme here is transmembrane solute handling in polarized epithelia of liver and kidney, coupled to regulated vesicular secretion. Several members are plasma-membrane carriers that set how nutrients and ions cross epithelial barriers: GLUT2 moves glucose across hepatocyte and beta-cell membranes and underlies glucose sensing, the organic cation transporter SLC22A2 clears cationic drugs and metabolites in the proximal tubule, SLC6A13 imports betaine and GABA, and the copper-transporting ATPase ATP7B loads copper onto ceruloplasmin and excretes excess into bile, its loss causing Wnson disease. LRP2/megalin retrieves filtered proteins and vitamin carriers by receptor-mediated endocytosis. Alongside these, Rab and active-zone-associated trafficking proteins direct granule and vesicle fusion, while the plasmin inhibitor SERPINF2 restrains fibrinolysis. Together the genes touch nutrient uptake, metal and xenobiotic excretion, and stimulus-coupled release.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: Cell migration and invasion are held in check by regulators that limit Rho-family GTPase activity and remodel the actin cytoskeleton, and several members here converge on that control point. ARHGAP5 accelerates GTP hydrolysis on RhoA, HACE1 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that targets active Rac1 for degradation, and SCAI restrains transcription-coupled invasion programmes, while JMY nucleates actin and also acts as a transcriptional cofactor for p53-dependent responses. Alongside these sit developmental transcription factors of the homeobox and NK2 families that specify regional and organ identity, notably NKX2-1 in thyroid and lung epithelium, plus APP and a chemokine ligand that influence adhesion and leukocyte recruitment. Taken together the grouping speaks to cytoskeletal and transcriptional restraint of motility and growth, biology whose loss contributes to tumour invasion and metastasis.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This is a loosely connected housekeeping module whose members support cell growth control, membrane and organelle dynamics, and the damping of stress signalling rather than one linear route. Several components sit downstream of DNA damage and proliferative cues: cyclin G1 is a p53-responsive regulator of cell cycle progression and PP2A recruitment, BMI1 is a Polycomb repressive complex 1 subunit that silences the CDKN2A locus and sustains stem and progenitor self-renewal, and NEK7 serves both mitotic spindle assembly and inflammasome activation. Others handle infrastructure: ADD3 caps and links spectrin cytoskeleton at membranes, RAP1B controls integrin-mediated adhesion, SLC25A46 shapes mitochondrial and ER membrane dynamics with mutations causing optic atrophy and neuropathy, PLEKHF2 acts on endosomes, and RNF11 is a ubiquitin ligase component restraining NF-κB. CMPK1 supplies pyrimidine nucleotide phosphorylation for DNA and RNA synthesis and for activating nucleoside analogue drugs.

candidates.name: regulation of transcription, transcription factors
candidates.description: A heterogeneous collection of transcriptional regulators and cofactors that set how RNA polymerase machinery is recruited and how much messenger RNA a gene yields, the layer of control that distinguishes one cell type from another and that tumours and developmental disorders routinely subvert. Several members act directly at promoters: BDP1 is a subunit of the RNA polymerase III initiation factor TFIIIB, BTAF1 modulates TBP binding to DNA, and MED23 is a Mediator subunit that couples signal-responsive activators to the core polymerase II apparatus. Others regulate transcription indirectly, through cyclin T2 in the CDK9-containing elongation kinase, CLK kinases that phosphorylate SR splicing factors, chromatin and cohesin-associated proteins such as ARID4B and STAG2, and zinc-finger and bZIP-type DNA-binding factors. Together they illustrate how initiation, elongation and co-transcriptional RNA processing are regulated as one connected process.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This grouping centres on membrane lipid organisation and the trafficking and signalling events built on it. Its clearest core is the aminophospholipid flippase machinery: ATP11B, a P4-ATPase, must partner with the accessory subunit TMEM30A (CDC50A) to fold, reach the plasma membrane and translocate phosphatidylserine to the cytosolic leaflet, which keeps this lipid hidden until apoptosis or platelet activation exposes it. LPGAT1 extends the theme by remodelling acyl chains during phospholipid synthesis, so bilayer composition and curvature are set here. The remaining members act on membrane-associated traffic and signal relay — STXBP3 in vesicle docking, SPAST in microtubule severing needed for membrane tubule and axonal maintenance, RP2 as a regulator of the small GTPase ARL3 in ciliary transport, and SOS2, PIK3CG, TGFBR1 and the IKK-family kinase CHUK transducing receptor signals from the membrane toward growth and inflammatory transcription.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: A loose assembly of housekeeping functions centred on nuclear gene expression and genome integrity, with additional arms in metabolism and membrane traffic. Transcription and chromatin components dominate: the Paf1-complex subunit CTR9 and the Elongator catalytic subunit ELP3 support RNA polymerase II elongation and co-transcriptional modification, GTF2H1 anchors the TFIIH complex used for both promoter opening and nucleotide-excision repair, and CSRP2BP contributes histone acetyltransferase activity. Genome maintenance is represented by the mismatch-repair protein PMS1, whose loss drives microsatellite instability, and by POT1, which caps the single-stranded telomeric overhang and prevents inappropriate DNA damage signalling at chromosome ends. Alongside these, ACADM performs the first step of medium-chain fatty acid beta-oxidation, ALG6 and nucleotide-sugar transporters serve glycosylation in the ER and Golgi, HPS5 builds lysosome-related organelles, and ATG4C processes autophagy proteins. Deficiencies in these genes produce unrelated disorders rather than one syndrome.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: Androgen receptor signalling toward luminal secretory epithelial identity is the coherent theme here, together with a minority of neuronal components. AR itself is a ligand-activated nuclear receptor whose transcriptional output specifies prostate luminal cells and drives their secretory programme; it is the therapeutic target in prostate cancer, and loss-of-function mutation causes androgen insensitivity. Alongside it sit transcription factors that pattern epithelia and glandular tissue components: SPDEF, which promotes secretory and goblet-cell differentiation, SOX9, required for chondrogenesis and ductal epithelium, and TFAP2A, acting in neural crest and surface ectoderm. SFN (14-3-3 csigma) links the group to p53-dependent growth arrest in stratified epithelia, while GRIN2B, KCNC3, NOS1AP and REEP1 reflect neuronal excitability and axonal membrane biology, genes mutated in spinocerebellar ataxia and hereditary spastic paraplegia. Hormone-responsive transcriptional control of differentiation is the unifying purpose.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: No single process unites these genes; they sample several unrelated areas of biology, and the most useful reading is of the parts. Two type I interferon alpha genes encode secreted cytokines that place cells in an antiviral state through JAK-STAT signalling and shape innate and adaptive immune responses. MST1 encodes macrophage-stimulating protein, a plasminogen-related ligand for the RON receptor tyrosine kinase that influences macrophage motility and epithelial responses, and its variants associate with inflammatory bowel disease. ESCO2 is an acetyltransferase that modifies the cohesin complex to establish sister chromatid cohesion during S phase, and its loss causes Roberts syndrome. LBX1 and POU4F2 are homeodomain and POU transcription factors directing neuronal and muscle precursor fate, while RNF17 acts in germ cell piRNA-dependent silencing. Several remaining entries are non-coding or poorly characterised loci.

candidates.name: transmembrane and ion transporters (II)
candidates.description: A mixed group of membrane transport and excitability proteins that set ion gradients and electrical signalling across several tissues. Included are voltage-gated and ligand-gated channels (a retinal calcium channel subunit, an atrial potassium channel, a kainate-type glutamate receptor), solute carriers that move calcium, sodium, bicarbonate and glutamate, and a copper-transporting ATPase whose loss causes hepatic and neurological copper overload in Wilson disease. Others shape the membrane environment in which channels work: junctophilin couples surface membrane to sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release in cardiomyocytes, and dystrophin anchors the sarcolemma to the cytoskeleton, with its loss producing muscular dystrophy. Together these activities support cardiac and skeletal muscle contraction, photoreceptor and synaptic transmission, glutamate clearance, and intracellular pH and metal homeostasis, and mutations in individual members give rise to arrhythmia, retinal dystrophy and ataxia.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This grouping centres on transcriptional repression and chromatin-based silencing, the machinery that keeps developmental and proliferative genes switched off until they are needed. Polycomb components are the anchor: BMI1 is a core subunit of the PRC1 ubiquitin ligase complex that marks histone H2A to maintain silencing, while AEBP2 is a zinc-finger accessory factor that helps target the companion PRC2 methyltransferase to chromatin. Other members add repressive and regulatory context — MIER3 acts as a transcriptional corepressor, CRY1 represses the transcriptional output of the circadian clock, CCNC pairs with CDK8 in the Mediator kinase module, and CDKN2AIP links to p53/ARF-dependent growth control. Together these activities bear on stem and progenitor self-renewal, cell cycle exit and senescence; loss of Polycomb repression releases the CDKN2A locus and other targets, a route to both premature senescence and cancer.

candidates.name: enriched for TF motif TNCATNTCCYR
candidates.description: A promoter-motif-defined grouping rather than a curated process: these genes share an upstream sequence resembling TNCATNTCCYR, the kind of shared cis-element that suggests coordinate transcriptional control by a common factor. The members converge on genome maintenance and basal transcription. RAD50 works within the sensor complex that detects double-strand breaks and initiates end resection, RAD51C supports homologous recombination and is a hereditary breast and ovarian cancer gene, and SMARCAL1 is an annealing helicase that stabilises stalled replication forks, its loss causing Schimke immuno-osseous dysplasia. GTF2H1 is a core general transcription factor subunit also used in nucleotide excision repair, ELP4 belongs to the Elongator complex, and MEN1 encodes the menin tumour suppressor that scaffolds chromatin-modifying complexes. Others contribute peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation, nucleotide signalling and vesicle tethering, so the set is best read as a regulatory module inferred from shared promoter architecture.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: No single canonical route unites these genes; what they share is a bias toward developmental patterning and tissue-specific differentiation programmes. BMP4 is the signalling anchor, a secreted TGF-beta family ligand that instructs dorsoventral and organ-field patterning, limb and skeletal morphogenesis, and epithelial-mesenchymal dialogue. Acting with it are homeodomain regulators of positional identity along the body axis (HOXB13, HOXD10), the forkhead factor FOXN1 that specifies thymic epithelium and hair/nail keratinocytes and is required for T cell development, and the transcriptional repressor PRDM8 together with the neuronal RNA-binding protein ELAVL3, both tied to nervous system maturation. Other members point to differentiated cell functions: junctophilin-2 couples sarcolemmal and sarcoplasmic reticulum membranes in cardiomyocyte calcium release, BOK belongs to the BCL-2 family governing apoptotic commitment, and a secreted phospholipase and beta-crystallin serve immune and lens roles respectively.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: The dominant theme here is nuclear RNA production and maturation: an RNA polymerase I subunit supports ribosomal RNA transcription, a small-subunit processome component participates in pre-rRNA processing toward ribosome assembly, a general transcription factor subunit assists RNA polymerase II promoter opening, a spliceosome-associated crooked-neck-like factor acts in pre-mRNA splicing, and a core exosome subunit provides 3' to 5' exoribonuclease-mediated RNA trimming and surveillance; loss of that exosome subunit causes cerebellar hypoplasia with spinal motor neuron degeneration. Together these activities set the cell's capacity for ribosome biogenesis and accurate mRNA output, and hence growth and protein synthesis. Accompanying members broaden the picture: a substrate receptor for a cullin-RING ubiquitin ligase couples protein degradation to this machinery, GTPase-of-immunity-associated proteins regulate lymphocyte survival, a SNARE contributes to Golgi vesicle fusion, and zinc-finger proteins add transcriptional regulation.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This is a heterogeneous grouping rather than a coherent signalling route, and the biology it points to is best read gene by gene. Several members are primate-specific TBC1D3 paralogues, products of a hominoid-expanded segmental duplication that carry a Rab-GAP-like domain, localise to endosomal membranes and modulate growth factor receptor trafficking and macropinocytosis; their amplification has been linked to transforming activity. CALCA encodes the precursor for calcitonin and CGRP, hormones that lower blood calcium and drive potent vasodilation and nociceptive signalling. PAN2 is the catalytic subunit of the Pan2-Pan3 deadenylase that trims mRNA poly(A) tails during the first phase of mRNA turnover, while CCNL2 is a cyclin-like partner of CDK11 acting in pre-mRNA splicing, so RNA processing and decay form one recognisable thread. AHSA2 is a co-chaperone-family relative of Hsp90 activators, with additional uncharacterised loci also included.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes converge on the braking and tuning of growth-factor signalling as it feeds into transcription, a control layer whose loss produces overgrowth, cancer and neurodevelopmental disease. Two GTPase-activating proteins, RASA2 for Ras and ACAP2 for an Arf-family GTPase, terminate signalling at the membrane, while MAP3K2 relays kinase input downstream and sorting nexins SNX13 and SNX14 govern endosomal trafficking and receptor fate. In the nucleus, the CREBBP acetyltransferase and the Mediator subunit MED1 couple activated signals to RNA polymerase II, and the NF-kappaB family member REL drives inflammatory and lymphoid transcription. Degradative and phosphorylation-based control comes from the FBXW7 ubiquitin ligase substrate receptor, which destroys short-lived growth regulators, and the DYRK1A kinase; STRN3 links the module to striatin-containing phosphatase complexes and Hippo pathway output. Many members are recurrently mutated in developmental disorders and tumours.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This grouping centres on the housekeeping machinery that keeps mitochondria energetically competent while proteins and metabolites are turned over. Two accessory subunits of respiratory complex I sit alongside the mitochondrial translation elongation factor TUFM, which delivers aminoacyl-tRNAs to the mitoribosome and so supplies the organelle-encoded core of the respiratory chain; PRELID1 participates in phospholipid transfer between mitochondrial membranes, and TMEM160 is an inner-membrane protein. Balancing these are degradative and biosynthetic functions: a proteasome beta subunit for ubiquitin-dependent turnover, the ER membrane protein BCAP31 that chaperones newly made membrane proteins and links to apoptotic signalling, APRT for adenine salvage into nucleotides, spermidine synthase for polyamine production, and tubulin cofactor B for tubulin folding. Together these represent the metabolic and proteostatic baseline on which oxidative ATP production, cytoskeletal assembly and cell growth depend.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes converge on cyclic AMP as an intracellular messenger and on the cells that depend on it. Two calcium/calmodulin-stimulated adenylate cyclases, ADCY1 and ADCY8, generate cAMP in neurons in response to calcium entry, coupling synaptic activity to kinase signalling and long-term potentiation; the serotonin receptor HTR6 and a G protein gamma subunit sit upstream of the same second-messenger route, while CAMK2N1 restrains calcium/calmodulin-dependent kinase II and so tunes the calcium arm of the response. In kidney collecting duct, the vasopressin receptor AVPR2 uses cAMP to drive aquaporin-mediated water reabsorption, and its loss causes nephrogenic diabetes insipidus. Other members act in muscle and germ cells, including a maternal-effect subcortical complex component and a tubulin-modifying enzyme, so the collection spans cAMP-dependent neuromodulation, water balance, and cell-type-specific cytoskeletal and developmental functions.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: No single physiological programme unites these genes; the group is best read as a loose collection spanning lipid storage, growth-factor feedback, small RNA transcription and nutrient transport, several of whose members remain uncharacterised open reading frames or polymerase-related pseudogene sequences. The better-defined components point to distinct processes: a perilipin-family protein coats lipid droplets and governs regulated triglyceride mobilisation in oxidative tissues such as heart and muscle; a TGF-β- and androgen-inducible membrane protein acts in negative feedback on that signalling and is frequently overexpressed in prostate cancer; a Ras-association domain protein of the tumour-suppressor family couples Ras signalling to apoptosis; a sodium-coupled transporter carries short-chain fatty acids and lactate across the intestinal and renal epithelium; and a subunit of the snRNA-activating protein complex drives transcription of the spliceosomal snRNA genes. Shared membership here reflects co-expression or genomic proximity rather than a common mechanism.

candidates.name: enriched in nuclear pore complex interacting proteins
candidates.description: Nuclear pore complex interacting proteins are a primate-expanded family encoded near segmental duplications on human chromosome 16, and the grouping here is built around them together with a scattering of other loci. The NPIP-related members associate with the nucleoporin scaffold that forms the gateway between nucleus and cytoplasm, the channel through which mRNA, ribosomal subunits and transcription factors pass and through which nucleocytoplasmic traffic is regulated; their duplication history makes them useful markers of recent genome rearrangement rather than of a single defined biochemical step. The remaining members belong to unrelated processes — LIN28A is an RNA-binding regulator of let-7 microRNA maturation and stem cell self-renewal, IL17A a T cell cytokine driving mucosal inflammation, HRH4 a histamine receptor on immune cells — so the set is best read as a duplication-defined locus group with limited shared function.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This grouping brings together proteins that have in common little more than a shared place in interaction screens, yet several of them converge on mitotic and genome-maintenance functions. SSNA1 is a microtubule-associated protein that promotes filament branching and localises to centrosomes and the midbody, and RASSF7 is likewise a centrosomal Ras-association domain protein required for orderly spindle formation and mitotic entry. Ubiquitin-dependent control is represented by E4F1, an atypical E3 ligase and transcription factor that acts on p53 and couples cell-cycle progression to metabolism, and by FBXL15, a substrate-recognition subunit of an SCF-type ligase. FAAP100 (C17orf70) belongs to the Fanconi anaemia core complex that ubiquitinates FANCD2 during interstrand crosslink repair, while TBL3 is a WD-repeat factor in small-subunit ribosome biogenesis. Together they mark proliferation-linked processes: spindle assembly, protein turnover, DNA crosslink repair and ribosome production.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes converge on the fat cell as a lipid-storing endocrine organ. Leptin is the adipocyte-derived hormone that reports fat mass to hypothalamic circuits controlling appetite and energy expenditure, and its loss causes severe hyperphagic obesity. CIDEC and PLIN4 act at the lipid droplet surface, the former promoting droplet fusion into the single large droplet characteristic of white adipocytes and the latter coating droplets to govern access by lipases; mutations in CIDEC cause partial lipodystrophy with insulin resistance. CD300LG is an endothelial transmembrane protein linked to triglyceride and HDL handling, TIMP4 restrains matrix metalloproteinases during adipose tissue remodelling, and HS2ST1 sulfates heparan sulfate chains that anchor lipases and growth factors to the cell surface. Together the group describes how triglyceride storage capacity, tissue expansion and metabolic signalling are coordinated, and how their failure produces dyslipidaemia and diabetes.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes define the differentiated intestinal epithelium, the absorptive lineage that lines the small bowel and colon and carries out nutrient uptake, barrier maintenance and fluid balance. The programme is set by a transcription factor core in which CDX1 and CDX2 specify intestinal identity and HNF4A and HNF4G drive enterocyte maturation; loss or ectopic activation of these factors underlies intestinal metaplasia and is used to distinguish gut-derived tumours. Downstream targets build the brush border and apical junctions, including villin, the atypical cadherins CDH17 and CDHR5, and the actin-based motor MYO1A, while FABP1 handles fatty acid transport, HMGCS2 supports ketogenesis from luminal substrates, and GUCY2C signals through cyclic GMP to control intestinal secretion. IL22RA1 places these cells downstream of mucosal cytokine signalling, and A1CF supports tissue-specific mRNA editing.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This grouping describes the differentiated absorptive epithelium of the intestine and liver, the tissue that takes up nutrients, forms a selective barrier, and performs first-pass metabolism of drugs and dietary xenobiotics. Its identity is set transcriptionally by the nuclear receptors HNF4A and HNF4G, which drive expression of brush border and apical junction components such as villin, CDHR5 and the harmonin scaffold USH1C, together with the lectin LGALS4 and the tetraspanin-like TM4SF5. A second arm is biotransformation: CYP3A4, CYP3A5 and CYP3A7 oxidise a large share of clinically used drugs, while a UDP-glucuronosyltransferase conjugates them for excretion, and A1CF contributes to mRNA editing characteristic of enterohepatic tissue. Loss of this programme underlies impaired barrier function and inflammatory bowel disease susceptibility, and variation in the CYP3A genes is a major source of interindividual differences in drug clearance.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes mark the differentiated intestinal and hepatic epithelium and the transcriptional programme that specifies it. HNF4A and HNF4G, with FOXA3, act as master regulators of enterocyte and hepatocyte identity, driving expression of the brush-border and junctional machinery that makes an absorptive epithelium possible: villin as the microvillar actin-bundling protein, claudin-2 setting paracellular cation and water permeability in the proximal intestine, and harmonin (USH1C) organising apical scaffolds. Others reflect specialised epithelial output, including galectin-4 in mucosal glycan handling, the mRNA-editing complementation factor A1CF acting with APOBEC1 on apolipoprotein B, DDC in amine synthesis, and CCL15 recruiting leukocytes to the gut mucosa. Loss of this regulatory axis impairs nutrient absorption and barrier function, and its reactivation or silencing accompanies colorectal and hepatic tumour differentiation states.

candidates.name: KLF12 targets network
candidates.description: KLF12 is a Kruppel-like zinc finger transcription factor that represses target promoters through GC-rich binding sites, and the genes assembled here represent its downstream regulatory output rather than a single biochemical route. The collection is functionally mixed, which is typical of a transcription factor target network: small GTPases and their partners (GNAI2, GNB2, RHOG) with an Arf GAP and endosomal sorting components point to heterotrimeric G protein signalling and membrane traffic; CORO1A and DGKZ tie into actin remodelling and lipid second messenger control in leukocytes; PPP2R1A, CNOT3 and UBE2M place phosphatase, mRNA deadenylation and neddylation-dependent protein turnover under the same regulatory umbrella. Also included are a nuclear liver X receptor partner and a latent TGF-beta binding protein, linking the network to lipid-sensing and extracellular growth factor availability. KLF12 activity has been studied in epithelial proliferation, cardiac and renal development, and tumour cell behaviour.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: A heterogeneous grouping of housekeeping regulators that link membrane traffic, chromatin-based transcriptional repression, and reversible protein modification. Clathrin-mediated endocytosis is represented by the AP-2 mu subunit and dynamin-2, whose GTPase-driven scission releases coated vesicles and whose loss impairs receptor uptake and causes myopathy and neuropathy. Chromatin and RNA regulation appear through HMG20B, a partner of the LSD1-CoREST demethylase corepressor complex, the transcription factor MAZ, the Groucho/TLE-family corepressor AES, and the hnRNP-type RNA-binding proteins RALY and ACIN1, the latter acting in splicing and in apoptotic chromatin condensation. Signalling output is tuned by serine/threonine phosphatase machinery, including the PP2A scaffolding A subunit and the PP1-targeting protein spinophilin, alongside the protein kinase PKN1 and the NEDD8-conjugating enzyme UBE2M, which primes cullin ubiquitin ligases. Together these activities support vesicle budding, gene silencing, and proteostasis rather than one linear route.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This grouping centres on the coupling of clathrin-mediated receptor internalisation to intracellular kinase signalling, the step that determines how long a growth factor signal lasts and whether the receptor is recycled or degraded. Adaptor and scission components, including the AP-2 mu subunit and dynamin-2, capture cargo at the plasma membrane and pinch off vesicles, while the ESCRT-0 protein HGS sorts ubiquitinated receptors toward the lysosome. On the signalling side, AKT1 and the related kinase PKN1 transmit survival and cytoskeletal cues, CDC37 works with HSP90 to fold and stabilise client kinases, and the scaffolding subunit of protein phosphatase 2A opposes them by dephosphorylation. TGFB1 provides a ligand whose receptors are themselves controlled by endocytic trafficking. Together these activities set signal amplitude and duration, processes that when deregulated drive growth factor independence in cancer and fibrotic tissue remodelling.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This is a mixed regulatory module centred on growth control, chromatin and protein turnover rather than a single linear route. Its clearest axis is nutrient- and energy-sensing restraint of cell growth: the kinase STK11 (LKB1) acts upstream of AMPK signalling, and TSC2 is the GTPase-activating component that switches off Rheb and thereby mTORC1, with EIF4G1 representing the cap-binding translation initiation step that mTORC1 ultimately controls. Loss of either tumour suppressor causes hamartoma syndromes and predisposes to cancer. A second strand concerns protein and receptor fate: HGS sorts ubiquitinated receptors into multivesicular bodies for lysosomal degradation, while UBE2M (UBC12) conjugates NEDD8 to cullins and DCAF15 serves as a substrate receptor for a cullin-RING ligase. MAP2K2 provides MEK-ERK mitogenic input, and BRD2 and the linker histone variant H1FX place part of this regulation on chromatin.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: No single mechanism unites these genes; they are better read as a collection of tissue-restricted and developmentally regulated products drawn from several unrelated processes. One recurring theme is epithelial and mucosal defence: alpha-defensin 5 is the antimicrobial peptide secreted by intestinal Paneth cells, a secretory protein of upper airway glands contributes to innate protection of mucosal surfaces, a colonic CEACAM adhesion molecule marks differentiated gut epithelium, and a type I interferon gene belongs to the antiviral response. A second theme is patterning and growth control, with posterior HOXC transcription factors specifying axial position, a Sprouty family member damping receptor tyrosine kinase output, and an imprinted zinc-finger gene acting in growth regulation. The remainder cover solute transport, including cystine import that sustains glutathione synthesis and ferroptosis resistance, plus chromatin, cytoskeletal and membrane-shaping components.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: No single coherent process unites these genes; they span secreted signalling, metal handling, steroid synthesis, muscle structure and mucosal defence, so the grouping is best read as a heterogeneous collection rather than one mechanism. Individual members do have well-defined roles: ATP7B loads copper onto ceruloplasmin and excretes excess copper into bile, and its loss causes Wilson disease with hepatic and neurological copper overload; CYP11B1 performs the final 11-beta-hydroxylation step of cortisol synthesis in the adrenal cortex, and its deficiency produces congenital adrenal hyperplasia; DMD encodes dystrophin, the sarcolemmal link between cytoskeleton and extracellular matrix whose absence causes muscular dystrophy. Others contribute to neuropeptide signalling through the pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating peptide, ERBB4 receptor tyrosine kinase signalling, Paneth cell antimicrobial defence, imprinted growth control, and type I interferon antiviral responses.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: The dominant theme here is neuronal specification and neurotrophic signalling, with several components that shape how developing neurons find their targets and survive. A secreted neuropeptide of the PACAP family acts through G protein-coupled receptors to promote neuronal survival and neuroendocrine responses to stress; a GDNF-family co-receptor transmits artemin signals in sensory and sympathetic neurons; ERBB4 receives neuregulin at synapses and in interneuron development; the delta-2 glutamate receptor subunit is a Purkinje cell synaptic organiser whose loss causes ataxia; and POU4F2 is the transcription factor that commits retinal ganglion cells to their fate. A beta-tubulin isotype supplies the microtubule lattice for axonal structure, and a cystine/glutamate antiporter links glutamate handling to glutathione synthesis and ferroptosis resistance. Other members, including an imprinted zinc-finger regulator, a Paneth cell defensin and a renal anion transporter, sit outside this neural core.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: This is a heterogeneous grouping whose members share little beyond being tissue-restricted effectors and regulators of differentiated cell function, so it is best read as a composite of developmental patterning and organ-specific specialisation rather than a single mechanism. Transcriptional regulators dominate one side of it: TFAP2A directs neural crest and surface ectoderm derivatives such as craniofacial structures and epidermis, HOXC10 contributes positional identity along the posterior body axis, and the imprinted PEG3 acts in growth control and maternal behaviour. Receptor signalling makes up another arm, with the Eph receptor EPHB1 guiding axons and cell sorting and ERBB4 responding to neuregulins in neural and cardiac development, while NPR3 clears natriuretic peptides and thereby tunes blood pressure and skeletal growth. The remainder are terminal specialisations: dystrophin anchoring the muscle sarcolemma, CYP11B1 completing adrenal cortisol synthesis, and DEFA5 providing Paneth cell antimicrobial defence in the small intestine.

candidates.name: ATF targets network
candidates.description: This is a set of candidate downstream targets of the ATF/CREB family of basic-leucine-zipper transcription factors, which bind cAMP- and stress-response elements to convert signals such as raised cAMP, endoplasmic reticulum stress and amino acid deprivation into changes in gene expression. Rather than a single biochemical route, the collection describes a transcriptional output: what the cell builds once these factors are engaged. Many of the members are neural or neuroendocrine, including the pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating neuropeptide ADCYAP1, which itself feeds back onto cAMP signalling, the brain lipid-binding protein FABP7 of radial glia and astrocytes, the brain-enriched sulfotransferase SULT4A1, and the endoplasmic reticulum-shaping protein REEP1 whose loss causes hereditary spastic paraplegia. Others cover copper export by ATP7B, Wnt-linked cytoskeletal control by DAAM2, imprinted growth regulation by PEG3 and positional patterning by HOXC10, indicating a regulatory network touching differentiation, metal handling and secretory signalling.

candidates.name: TBA
candidates.description: These genes outline the myeloid identity and activation program of monocytes and macrophages, the cells that patrol tissue for microbes and debris and set the tone of an inflammatory response. The transcription factor SPI1 (PU.1) specifies this lineage together with HHEX, while TLR4 senses bacterial lipopolysaccharide and PTAFR responds to platelet-activating factor, coupling through the Src-family kinase LYN, the phospholipase PLCB2 and the ITAM-bearing adaptor TYROBP (DAP12) to calcium mobilization and cytoskeletal change; DOK2 acts as a brake on this kinase signaling. Scavenger and lipoprotein receptors such as STAB1 and APOB48R support clearance of modified ligands and lipid uptake, linking the same cells to foam cell formation in atherosclerosis. TNFSF13 (APRIL) released by these cells feeds back on B cell survival and immunoglobulin production, tying innate activation to humoral immunity.

candidates.name: TBA
