Its failure is the basis of axonal degeneration and dying-back neuropathy, and several of the genes here are classical neurodegeneration loci: mutations in the dynactin subunit DCTN1 cause motor neuron disease, presenilin and amyloid precursor protein are central to Alzheimer pathology, the prion protein supports peripheral myelinated axon integrity, and defects in the peroxisomal transporter ABCD1 produce adrenoleukodystrophy with long-tract axonopathy. Mechanistically the contributions are heterogeneous: microtubule binding and dynein-based transport along the process, an ion pump that sustains the axonal membrane potential, lipid handling, and trophic input through insulin and ephrin receptor signalling.

candidates.name: regulation of T-helper 17 cell lineage commitment
candidates.description: Naive CD4 T cells can be steered toward the Th17 fate, and this regulatory layer sets how readily that happens. Th17 cells defend mucosal barriers against fungi and extracellular bacteria through IL-17 production, but excessive commitment drives psoriasis, inflammatory bowel disease and other autoimmune inflammation, which is why IL-23 blockade is therapeutically effective. The genes here act at several levels: the IL-23 receptor and its shared IL-12 family subunits deliver the extracellular cue, JAK3 and STAT proteins transduce it, and the bromodomain readers BRD2 and BRD4 together with the acetyltransferase EP300 open or restrain the relevant enhancers. Opposing lineage signals also appear, since TBX21 specifies the Th1 programme and STAT5A signalling favours regulatory T cell differentiation, so commitment reflects a balance among competing transcriptional programmes rather than a single instructive switch.

candidates.name: negative regulation of lymphocyte migration
candidates.description: Lymphocytes only work if they stop moving at the right moment, and this pathway covers the braking signals that hold them in place or damp their recruitment. Retention in lymphoid tissue after activation, restraint of inflammatory infiltration, and the maintenance of immune quiescence in tissues such as the CNS all depend on it; losing these brakes contributes to excessive tissue infiltration and autoimmune damage. The mechanisms are mixed: CD69 on newly activated cells antagonises sphingosine-1-phosphate-driven egress, CD200 engaging its receptor CD200R1 delivers an inhibitory cue from surrounding tissue, and cytoskeletal regulators including RIPOR2, LRCH1 and WASL act on RhoA signalling and actin branching to limit chemokine-driven polarisation and adhesion. Kinase signalling through AKT1 and cytokine input via IL27RA tune the response, placing this biology at the intersection of leukocyte chemotaxis, adhesion and immune tolerance.

candidates.name: negative regulation of motor neuron apoptotic process
candidates.description: Motor neurons are generated in excess during development and pruned by programmed cell death, so the survival signals that block motor neuron apoptosis determine how many reach and maintain their muscle targets. Loss of this restraint underlies motor neuron degeneration, and the same suppression keeps mature neurons alive after axonal injury. Trophic input contributes through a secreted cytokine-like factor of the cardiotrophin-like family that acts on motor neuron survival receptors, while a stress-kinase axis of the JNK cascade sets the threshold for death, with the mixed-lineage kinase MAP3K12 acting through MAP2K4 as a pro-apoptotic and axon-degeneration relay that must be held in check. Vesicle trafficking and nuclear body components also figure here, as defects in the retromer-associated VPS54 and in ZPR1 produce motor neuron loss in models of degenerative motor disease, linking neuronal survival to protein transport and RNA-related housekeeping.

candidates.name: negative regulation of integrin-mediated signaling pathway
candidates.description: Integrin signalling has to be turned down as well as on, and negative regulation of the integrin-mediated signaling pathway covers the processes that limit how strongly cells read and respond to the extracellular matrix. Damping this input matters for controlling adhesion strength, cell migration speed and matrix remodelling: cells that cannot restrain integrin output adhere and spread inappropriately, which affects wound healing, vascular wall integrity and tumour invasiveness. The contributing activities are varied rather than a single cascade — a phosphatase-targeting regulator restrains the actin-based responses that follow integrin engagement, a serine protease inhibitor blocks plasminogen activation and competes for matrix-binding sites used for adhesion, and an adherens junction catenin links cadherin-based contacts to the actin cytoskeleton in ways that oppose matrix adhesion signalling. Post-transcriptional repression by a microRNA adds a further layer of restraint on this signalling output.

candidates.name: negative regulation of CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell activation
candidates.description: Cytotoxic CD8-positive alpha-beta T cells kill infected and transformed cells, and restraining their activation is what keeps that killing proportionate and self-tolerant. Damping this response prevents autoimmune tissue destruction and immunopathology during infection, but the same brakes are exploited by tumours to evade immune attack, which is why several members here are the targets of checkpoint blockade. The mechanisms are mixed: PD-L1 and VISTA are inhibitory ligands engaging receptors on the T cell surface; LILRB1 and HFE act through MHC class I recognition; SOCS1 shuts down cytokine receptor signalling from inside the cell; and ZBTB7B (ThPOK) suppresses the CD8 cytotoxic programme during thymic lineage choice, favouring CD4 helper commitment. Together these constitute co-inhibitory signalling, cytokine-signalling attenuation and developmental repression converging on cytotoxic T cell output.

candidates.name: HCN channels
candidates.description: The four HCN subunits encode the hyperpolarization-activated, cyclic nucleotide-gated channels that carry the "funny" pacemaker current and set the rate of spontaneous firing in the heart and brain. Unusually, they open on hyperpolarization rather than depolarization, conducting a mixed inward Na+/K+ current in the diastolic voltage range that drives the slow depolarization taking a sinoatrial cell to its next action potential; direct cAMP binding to the channel's cyclic nucleotide-binding domain speeds activation, which is how sympathetic and vagal tone accelerate or slow the heart. HCN4 dominates in the sinoatrial node, with HCN1 and HCN2 prominent in neurons, where the same current shapes resting potential, dendritic integration and rhythmic burst firing. Loss-of-function mutations cause sinus bradycardia and arrhythmia, and HCN1 variants cause epilepsy; the cardiac current is the target of rate-lowering drugs such as ivabradine.

candidates.name: IP6 and IP7 transport between cytosol and nucleus
candidates.description: Highly phosphorylated inositols act as diffusible signals and phosphate donors inside the nucleus, where they influence chromatin regulation, mRNA export and transcription, so the cell must move inositol hexakisphosphate and the pyrophosphorylated form IP7 between cytosol and nucleus rather than making them only where they are used. This passage across the nuclear envelope is attributed to the nuclear pore complex, and the components here are its parts: the structural Y-complex scaffold with NUP107, NUP133, NUP85, SEC13 and SEH1L, the transmembrane ring anchors NDC1 and the POM121 proteins, the phenylalanine-glycine channel nucleoporins NUP62, NUP54 and NUP98 that form the permeability barrier, and peripheral elements such as NUP153, NUP50, RANBP2 and TPR on the cytoplasmic filaments and nuclear basket. How these small, densely charged metabolites are selected and translocated is not established, so the pathway is best read as the conduit rather than a defined carrier mechanism.

candidates.name: Miscellaneous substrates
candidates.description: Cytochrome P450 enzymes acting on miscellaneous substrates are those whose oxidative chemistry is demonstrable but whose physiological substrates and regulation remain incompletely defined, so they sit outside the tidy classes of steroid, bile acid or eicosanoid metabolism. Their importance is nonetheless concrete: CYP2D6 oxidises a large share of clinically used drugs and its polymorphisms drive interindividual differences in dose response, while CYP4F2 and CYP4A11 hydroxylate arachidonic acid and related lipids to influence vascular tone and blood pressure, and CYP4F22 is required for the ultra-long-chain fatty acid processing that builds the epidermal permeability barrier, with loss-of-function causing ichthyosis. Others, including CYP2S1, CYP2U1, CYP2W1 and CYP4B1, are expressed in epithelia, brain or tumours and perform monooxygenation of fatty acids and xenobiotics whose in vivo significance is still being established.

candidates.name: Insulin-like Growth Factor-2 mRNA Binding Proteins (IGF2BPs/IMPs/VICKZs) bind RNA
candidates.description: A small family of cytoplasmic RNA-binding proteins, IGF2BP1-3 (also called IMPs or VICKZs), grabs thousands of protein-coding transcripts and decides how long they survive, where in the cell they are translated, and how efficiently. This control matters most in contexts of rapid growth and movement: the proteins are highly expressed in embryonic tissues, guide localized translation of mRNAs such as beta-actin at the leading edge of migrating cells, and are re-expressed in many cancers, where they stabilize oncogenic messages including MYC and drive proliferation and invasion. Recognition depends on a CAUH sequence motif read by tandem KH domains, and binding generally shields the transcript from decay rather than silencing it. The imprinted noncoding RNA H19 is part of this circuitry, reflecting the family's link to the imprinted IGF2/H19 locus and to growth regulation.

candidates.name: Defective ABCB4 causes PFIC3, ICP3 and GBD1
candidates.description: Hepatocytes protect their own bile ducts by secreting phospholipid alongside bile salts, and ABCB4 (MDR3) is the canalicular floppase that performs this step, translocating phosphatidylcholine into bile in an ATP-dependent manner. The exported phospholipid forms mixed micelles with bile salts and cholesterol, blunting the detergent action of bile acids and keeping cholesterol in solution. When the transporter is defective, bile becomes phospholipid-poor and directly injurious: canalicular membranes and biliary epithelium are damaged, bile flow fails, and cholesterol crystallises. The resulting phenotypes span a spectrum of cholestatic liver disease, from progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis type 3 with early ductular injury and fibrosis, through the reversible intrahepatic cholestasis of the third trimester of pregnancy, to adult cholesterol gallstone disease. This places the transporter at the centre of bile formation, biliary lipid homeostasis and susceptibility to cholelithiasis.

candidates.name: RAB GEFs exchange GTP for GDP on RABs
candidates.description: RAB GTPases mark the identity of intracellular membranes, and they can only recruit effectors when loaded with GTP, so the exchange factors that swap GDP for GTP decide when and where a trafficking step happens. Activation converts a soluble GDI-bound RAB into a membrane-attached organizer of vesicle budding, motility, tethering and fusion, governing endocytosis, recycling, Golgi transport, autophagy and lysosome-related organelle biogenesis such as melanosome and granule formation. The exchange factors are structurally heterogeneous: DENN-domain proteins acting on RAB35 and others, VPS9-domain proteins including RABGEF1 and the RIN family that switch on RAB5, the multisubunit TRAPP complex serving RAB1, and heterodimers like RIC1:RGP1. Escort proteins CHM/CHML deliver newly prenylated RABs to membranes; loss of CHM causes choroideremia, and mutations in RAB3GAP and TRAPP subunits cause developmental and skeletal disease.

candidates.name: Gene and protein expression by JAK-STAT signaling after Interleukin-12 stimulation
candidates.description: Interleukin-12 drives naive CD4+ T cells toward the Th1 fate, and this pathway captures the gene and protein output of that instruction, transmitted through JAK-STAT signalling with STAT4 as the central transcription factor. The functional readouts are the hallmark Th1 cytokine IFNG alongside IL10, which together set the balance between cell-mediated immunity against intracellular pathogens and its restraint; loss of this axis leaves people prone to mycobacterial and salmonella infection, while excess activity contributes to autoimmune inflammation. Downstream of transcription, the proteomic response reorganises the cell rather than simply adding cytokines: actin and membrane cytoskeletal regulators such as cofilin, moesin, CDC42 and PAK2 shift with motility and immune synapse formation, heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoproteins and chaperonin subunits with altered RNA handling and folding load, and superoxide dismutases, peroxiredoxin-like and glutathione transferase activities with redox adjustment during lymphocyte activation and proliferation.

candidates.name: RHOV GTPase cycle
candidates.description: RHOV, also called Chp, is an atypical Rho-family GTPase that appears constitutively active because of unusually fast intrinsic nucleotide exchange; no exchange factors or GTPase-activating proteins specific to it are known, so its nucleotide cycle is set largely by its own chemistry and by the effectors it engages. Expressed at low levels and prominent in embryonic tissue, it acts downstream of WNT signalling in neural crest formation and shapes cell adhesion by influencing E-cadherin and beta-catenin at adherens junctions. Effector partners here include PAK kinases, the mixed-lineage kinase MAP3K11 and the adaptor SH3RF1 feeding JNK activation, alongside GIT/ARHGEF7 complexes, PAR6 polarity proteins, NCK adaptors, IQGAP1 and spectrin and tropomyosin components that link the GTPase to actin and junctional cytoskeleton. Signalling through this route can drive apoptosis in some cells, and RHOV overexpression marks lung adenocarcinoma, where it behaves as an oncogene.

candidates.name: NTF3 activates NTRK2 (TRKB) signaling
candidates.description: Neurotrophin-3 can engage TRKB, the receptor tyrosine kinase encoded by NTRK2, even though its preferred partner is TRKC and TRKB's high-affinity ligands are BDNF and NT-4. This low-affinity pairing belongs to the broader neurotrophin system that governs survival, differentiation and synaptic plasticity of neurons in the developing and adult nervous system, and it offers a route by which NT-3 secreted in a given territory can influence TRKB-bearing cells. Ligand binding promotes receptor dimerization and trans-autophosphorylation of conserved tyrosine residues in the cytoplasmic kinase domain, the step that normally creates docking sites for adaptors feeding into MAPK, PI3K/AKT and PLC-gamma cascades. Activation through this route is inefficient compared with BDNF-driven TRKB signaling, and the consequences downstream of it remain poorly characterized, so it is best read as a minor, cross-reactive arm of neurotrophin receptor activation.

candidates.name: Infection with Enterobacteria
candidates.description: Enterobacteriaceae are ordinary gut residents, yet pathogenic strains invade tissue, secrete toxins, and spread to the urinary tract, airways, peritoneum, meninges and bloodstream, making them a leading cause of diarrhoea, urinary tract infection, pneumonia and sepsis, increasingly hard to treat as resistance plasmids circulate. The host side of infection with enterobacteria shows up here as the surfaces bacteria grab and breach and the defences mounted against them: basement membrane and matrix components such as the collagen IV and laminin families, fibronectin, and epithelial proteins including EpCAM and a urothelial uroplakin serve as adhesion and invasion substrates for fimbriae and bacterial proteases. Against cytosolic bacteria and their lipopolysaccharide, guanylate-binding proteins coat pathogen-containing vacuoles and license caspase-4 to trigger inflammasome-driven pyroptosis, while ubiquitin and a conjugating enzyme support targeting of bacteria for degradation. Calmodulin and haemoglobin chains reflect toxin activation and iron acquisition during infection.

candidates.name: Defective Inhibition of DNA Recombination at Telomere Due to DAXX Mutations
candidates.description: Telomeres must be kept from engaging the homologous recombination machinery, and the ATRX-DAXX complex is one of the guards that enforces this. DAXX is the histone chaperone partner that, with the ATRX remodeller, deposits histone H3.3 into telomeric and pericentromeric heterochromatin, keeping the repeats packaged and suppressing recombination between them. When DAXX carries loss-of-function mutations, that chromatin deposition fails and telomeres become substrates for recombination-based copying, producing the alternative lengthening of telomeres phenotype: heterogeneous, elongated telomeres maintained without telomerase. This route to telomere maintenance is found in a subset of tumours, notably pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, sarcomas and gliomas, and accounts for cases with ALT hallmarks that lack ATRX lesions. The biology links histone variant chaperoning and heterochromatin maintenance directly to replicative immortality in cancer.

candidates.name: FLT3 signaling through SRC family kinases
candidates.description: FLT3 is a receptor tyrosine kinase on haematopoietic stem and progenitor cells that, on binding its ligand FLT3LG, drives survival and expansion of early myeloid and lymphoid precursors and dendritic cell development; activating FLT3 mutations are among the most common lesions in acute myeloid leukaemia and a target of kinase inhibitor therapy. One arm of its output runs through SRC family kinases, with FYN, HCK and LCK, together with the related kinase SYK, recruited to the activated receptor. Their contribution is mixed rather than uniformly stimulatory: some promote downstream signalling read out as increased STAT5 activation and proliferation, while others feed into ubiquitin ligase recruitment that attenuates the receptor by degradation. The pathway therefore sets both the strength and the duration of FLT3 signalling in normal progenitors and in leukaemic blasts.

candidates.name: Formation of WDR5-containing histone-modifying complexes
candidates.description: WDR5 is a scaffolding hub that nucleates chromatin-modifying assemblies, and this pathway covers how those complexes are built. WDR5 joins RBBP5, ASH2L and DPY30 to form the WRAD module that licenses and positions the six KMT2 methyltransferases (KMT2A-D, SETD1A, SETD1B), which deposit mono-, di- and trimethylation on histone H3 lysine 4 at active promoters and enhancers. Complex-specific partners diversify targeting: MEN1 and the protease TASP1 with KMT2A/B, KDM6A, NCOA6, PAXIP1 and PAGR1 with KMT2C/D, and CXXC1 with WDR82 in the SET1 complexes. WDR5 also sits in the GCN5/PCAF-ATAC and KAT8-NSL acetyltransferase complexes, linking H3K4 methylation to histone acetylation. This machinery sets Hox gene expression during embryonic patterning and lineage specification; germline loss causes chromatinopathies such as Kabuki and Wiedemann-Steiner syndromes, and KMT2A rearrangement drives mixed lineage leukemia, making the WDR5 interface a drug target.

candidates.name: Specification of the neural plate border
candidates.description: Between the future brain and the future skin, a strip of ectoderm is set aside that will become the neural crest and the cranial placodes; specifying this neural plate border is what allows vertebrates to build a peripheral nervous system, craniofacial skeleton, melanocytes, adrenal medulla, lens, inner ear and olfactory epithelium. The territory is defined positionally by intermediate levels of BMP and FGF with a graded WNT input, so that BMP4, FGF4 and WNT3A acting through beta-catenin and TCF7L1 place cells between neural and epidermal fates rather than in either. Within that domain a combination of transcription factors, including GBX2, TFAP2A and its paralogues, PAX3, PAX7, MSX1, DLX5 and ZIC1, cross-regulate into a self-reinforcing border identity while pluripotency factors are resolved. No single gene marks the border; failure here underlies neurocristopathies and craniofacial malformation.
